independence: same-family blind artifact critique; not a cross-family verdict

findings.title: Malformed YAML indentation is accepted as a green Forge
findings.evidence: An exact-commit fixture with `name: alpha` followed by a two-space-indented `description:` exited 0 with valid=true, errors=0, and no diagnostics. PyYAML 6.0.3 rejects the same mapping with `ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here`. In validate_skills.py:239-258, an indent increase is assigned to the current stack parent even when the preceding scalar did not open a mapping container, so invalid child indentation is silently flattened into the root mapping.
findings.recompute:
Extract commit a083552def772489ae238bf6931cd275d471b263; create one registered model skill whose SKILL.md frontmatter is `---
name: alpha
  description: A fixture. Use when testing. Differentiator - fixture.
---`; add a valid sidecar; run `python -B scripts/validate_skills.py --root <fixture> --json` and observe exit 0/valid true. Then pass `name: alpha
  description: invalid` to `yaml.safe_load` and observe ScannerError.

findings.title: A completely empty or erased Forge can pass 0/0
findings.evidence: A fixture containing only skills/registry.json with `{}` returned valid=true, skillsRegistered=0, skillsLoaded=0, errors=0, warnings=0, and no diagnostics. validate_skills.py:692 skips `_registry_entries()` whenever the decoded registry object is falsey, and no existential invariant requires a non-empty registry or any skill. Total skill deletion plus an emptied registry can therefore green the whole-Forge gate.
findings.recompute: Extract the reviewed commit; create `<fixture>/skills/registry.json` containing `{}` and no skill directories; run `python -B scripts/validate_skills.py --root <fixture> --json`; observe exit 0 and valid=true with 0/0 skills.

findings.title: One-hop validation does not require reference payloads to be directly reachable
findings.evidence: A valid one-skill fixture with references/orphan.md and no link to it from SKILL.md returned valid=true with no diagnostics. validate_skills.py:613-627 resolves links found in SKILL.md and rejects onward links found in reference files, but never compares references/* against the set of direct SKILL.md targets. This misses the canon requirement that each sibling reference be pointed to directly from SKILL.md.
findings.recompute: Create a passing registered skill and valid sidecar; add `references/orphan.md` without linking it from SKILL.md; run the reviewed validator in canonical mode and observe valid=true.

findings.title: Template-label heuristic suppresses validation of concrete unsafe targets
findings.evidence: A SKILL.md link `[<outside>](/definitely/absolute/missing.md)` returned valid=true with no diagnostics. validate_skills.py:577-590 classifies any label containing both angle brackets as a template before inspecting the concrete target, bypassing REFERENCE_ABSOLUTE and REFERENCE_MISSING. Template detection should be based on a demonstrably placeholder target, not only label punctuation.
findings.recompute: Create a passing registered skill and append `See [<outside>](/definitely/absolute/missing.md).` to SKILL.md; run canonical validation and observe valid=true instead of REFERENCE_ABSOLUTE.

notes: The artifact is dependency-free in implementation, produces clean machine-readable JSON, returns nonzero on detected errors, distinguishes canonical/Codex-strict/dated supplied claude.ai semantics honestly, and is red-capable across many representative defects. Approval is withheld because the parser and existential-registry holes allow the core validator to certify invalid or entirely absent source. Fix those critical false greens and add direct-reference reachability coverage before promotion.
